# Diónysos: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Diónysos** is what the evidence put back.

Diónysos is born twice, dies once, and comes back everywhere. His myths are stories of arrival — from the east, from the underworld, from the thigh of Zeus — and of the resistance he meets from those who fear losing control. Semele, daughter of Cadmus, asked Zeus to reveal himself in his full divine glory.  The sight killed her.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Diónysos
- **ASCII form:** dionysos
- **Meaning:** "God of Nysa (mountain of ecstasy)"
- **Domain of influence:** Wine, Ecstasy, Theatre
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** Διόνυσος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 69 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Διόνυσος**. On the evidence, it means "God of Nysa (mountain of ecstasy)".

Strip **Diónysos** to *dionysos* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ó** — Acute on omicron: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Diónysos** lives at [/sites/dionysos/](/sites/dionysos/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/dionysos/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/dionysos/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/dionysos/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Diónysos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Music, Arts & Performance** — Theatre was born at his festival; drama is his liturgy.
- **Wine, Brewing & Hospitality** — Wine, ecstasy, and the vine; the hospitality industry’s founding deity.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — His Bacchic mysteries swept the Roman world; the Senate outlawed them and failed.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/dionysos/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Diāna** ([read it here](/sites/diana/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Drákōn** ([read it here](/sites/drakon/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
